subject: Controller/Processor split and SCCs appendix — draft tie-out
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Catherine O'Neill <c.oneill@novacare.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-09T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Controller/Processor split and SCCs appendix — draft tie-out

Hi Catherine,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached are Redwood's redlines for the MSA (order form tie-out) and our proposed DPA + SCCs appendix. Key items where we need confirmation from Novacare legal:

- Section 2 (roles): we propose Novacare be Controller; Redwood remains Processor for model inference and logging. Confirm if you need a controller-controller carveout for customer-provided training data.
- Subprocessor flow and notices: we added a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors with a documented objection path.
- SCCs appendix: mapped to Annex II safeguards; we propose retaining EU hosting as fallback for data residency.
- Export controls / export licensing: proposing an export-control representation limited to Redwood-managed model outputs, not downstream customer uploads.

Please review the attached and flag the priority items. We'd like to align on language by end of next week to keep the pilot onboarding on track.

Attachments: RI_DPA_redline.docx, SCCs_Appendix_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Catherine O'Neill <c.oneill@novacare.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Novacare Legal <legal@novacare.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Controller/Processor split and SCCs appendix — draft tie-out

Jonas,

Thanks for the redline and the clear summary. We reviewed with our counsel this morning and have a couple of high-level responses: 

1) Roles: we generally agree with the controller/processor mapping but will need a limited controller-controller clause for customer uploads used for fine-tuning (Sec 2.3).
2) Subprocessors: 30-day notice is realistic, but Novacare needs a carveout to object for subprocessors handling PHI; can we add an expedited 7-day objection for those cases?
3) SCCs appendix: we prefer the language to map to the newer EU SCCs (2021) with a short exhibit showing safeguards rather than a long Annex II table.
4) Indemnity: our legal would like Redwood to accept a narrower indemnity for third-party claims arising from Redwood's subprocessor actions; suggest specific language.

I've attached our marked MSA for reference (Novacare_MSA_redline.pdf). We can do a 30-minute legal-only call tomorrow afternoon to walk the open items.

Catherine O'Neill
VP Legal, Novacare

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Novacare MSA redline (summary)

Thanks Jonas — read through the redline. High-level legal position and proposed next steps: 

- Roles/clause: maintain controller/processor baseline. For the fine-tuning carveout we can offer a short clause that requires explicit written instruction and a data processing addendum amendment when Novacare elects to have Redwood act as joint-controller for customer-provided training inputs. Draft: "Where Customer elects Redwood to process Customer-provided training data for model updates, Parties will document the scope and Controller/Joint-Controller allocation in a written addendum."
- Subprocesssors & PHI: agree to the 7-day expedited objection only where Processor will process PHI. We should define PHI by reference to HIPAA and EU special categories.
- SCCs: accept Novacare preference for the 2021 SCCs; propose a short exhibit that maps to our technical controls (Annex II style) but keeps the appendix concise.
- Indemnity: push back on unlimited third-party indemnity; propose negotiated cap tied to Order Form fees for first 12 months.

Next steps: I'll prepare a tracked mark with suggested language for the call. Recommend a 30-min legal sync (Novacare counsel + Laura + Jonas) tomorrow at 3pm BST / 7am PT.

I'll also draft responses we can share with Ben for procurement trade-offs.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novacare MSA redline (summary) — procurement note

Quick procurement note: if Novacare requires EU-only hosting as the default for the production environment we should expect a price uplift and a longer lead time for Dedicated capacity.

- Pricing: estimated +18-25% on hosting/OPEX for reserved capacity depending on region commitment length.
- SLA: regional SLOs may require a dedicated deployment lane; ops needs a 6-week lead to provision.
- Trade-offs: can offer EU-only fallback for regulated datasets while keeping global default for non-regulated testing workloads.

I'll prepare a short impact memo for the call and include options (price / timeline / fallbacks).

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
